    Ready,
    Doing,
    Review,
    Done,
    Blocked,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "UPPERCASE")]

    S,
    M,
    L,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct DocFront {
    pub id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub kind: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub status: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default = "default_order")]
    pub order: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub summary: Option<String>,

fn default_order() -> i64 {
    999

cards.title: Five stores and atomic storage
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Five persistent stores: identity.md, user.md, memory/, journal/, loops.md.
  • Plain Markdown; directories 0700, files 0600; write to a temporary file, then rename.
  • Memory split into preferences.md / lessons.md; one journal file per month, merged by day.
  • Civil dates computed in-tree, no timezone dependency.

Acceptance

  • Round-trip tests for all five stores.
  • Same-day journal appends merge; different days stay ordered.
  • Permissions verified as 0700 / 0600.
  • Missing identity.md returns None instead of a fabricated empty string.

Notes

Markdown is the only format: for a single user under 200 entries, files are the best query engine. Saving rewrites the layout, so hand-written comments may disappear; that is the accepted cost.

cards.title: Prompt assembly and in-band protocol
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Stable prefix: persona → identity → user → memory → protocol.
  • Volatile sections last: today → loops → journal.
  • Section budgets: 600 each for identity and user, 2000 for memory, 300 for loops, 600 for journal.
  • In-band protocol: <<niuse:memory>>, <<niuse:loop>>, <<niuse:journal>>.
  • Streaming strip needs a tail buffer; unterminated blocks stay visible.

Acceptance

  • Section order covered by a test; expired memory excluded; entries older than 30 days marked unverified.
  • Oversized identity is truncated and labelled.
  • Protocol tests cover blocks split across chunks, partial prefixes, false markers, and unterminated blocks.
  • In real calls the candidate block is stripped and the prose is intact.

Notes

The original plan had memory and loop blocks only. To avoid a second model call, a journal block was added and is written automatically.

cards.title: REPL and the niucode driver
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Interactive REPL: streaming output, slash commands, Ctrl-C cancel, Ctrl-D exit.
  • The driver opens or resumes thread.jsonl and rebuilds history with project_history.
  • Each turn sets the working directory again, proving per-turn cwd on one session.
  • Candidate confirmation: y / n / e / s; conflicts use r / k / d.

Acceptance

  • A real provider run completes a read-only task and persists the session.
  • The same session reads in one directory, /cd /tmp, then reads in another; both succeed.
  • Confirming a candidate writes memory that niuse mem list can show.
  • Journal and loop blocks are written automatically.
  • The driver is about 200 lines and does not bypass the loop.

Notes

niucode-cli is a binary with no library target, so its TUI and renderer cannot be reused. The MVP ships a minimal renderer and can swap later once upstream exposes a library or a hook.

cards.title: Soft expiry, conflicts, secret scan
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Normal injection within 30 days; unverified from 31 to 90; not injected after 90.
  • Conflict detection via character-bigram Jaccard: ≥ 0.5 is similar; same tag lowers the bar to 0.35.
  • Secret patterns: sk-, ghp_, github_pat_, AKIA, private-key blocks, Slack, Google, long hex.
  • Refusal is the default; the CLI needs --force to override.

Acceptance

  • Common key shapes match; ordinary Chinese prose and short hex do not.
  • Tests for similar, unrelated, and same-tag pairs.
  • A real sk-... input is refused with exit code 1.
  • Expired memory is excluded from the prompt.

Notes

Scanning is a backstop, not a guarantee. Private projects, client names, and internal addresses still rely on human judgement at confirmation time.

cards.title: Cold start and the review queue
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap [--limit N] [--since-days N] scans ~/.niucode/sessions.
  • Only user / assistant text is sent; tool output is dropped.
  • One tool-free extraction returns {kind, text, tags} and writes inbox.md.
  • niuse review walks the queue with y / n / s / q; accepted entries become memory.

Acceptance

  • Empty sessions are skipped; only sessions with dialogue cost a model call.
  • Candidates are deduplicated against existing memory and within the batch.
  • Inbox format has a round-trip test.
  • A real run mined a sandbox lesson that review accepted into memory.

Notes

Default cap is 40 sessions. Cost is roughly 2k input tokens per session, one-off.

cards.title: Architecture dashboard
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Reuse niucode's xtask generator and three-column shell, with a niuse project model.
  • Four views: Architecture (default), Work, Docs, Decisions.
  • Sources: project.json plus board/*.md plus docs/**/*.md.
  • Single-file docs/index.html, offline, no CDN, no runtime fetch.
  • cargo xtask dashboard --check fails when generated output is stale.

Acceptance

  • cargo xtask dashboard writes docs/index.html and model.json.
  • Validation passes: module paths exist, card references resolve, ADR statuses are legal.
  • Architecture shows modules, layers, and dependency arrows.
  • Docs opens the architecture doc, the plan, and both ADRs.
  • --check passes.

Notes

The board is read-only; state changes go through the repository so it never becomes a second source of truth. The generator is copied from niucode; only branding and the project model changed.

cards.title: Ten working days of dogfood
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • At least one real task per day goes through niuse, not niucode.
  • Record proposals, acceptances, and concrete cases where memory saved a round of explanation.
  • At least once it should disagree and change your mind.
  • Keep the store under 50 entries; more means the bar is too low.

Acceptance

  • Ten consecutive working days.
  • Candidate acceptance rate ≥ 60%.
  • At least 3 correct citations of a past judgement.
  • At least 1 case of being persuaded.
  • At least 1 A/B case where NIUSE_MEMORY=off changes the answer.

Notes

Record one row per day in the dogfood log. This card writes no code. Its job is to stop new features before the current ones are validated.

cards.title: Show a full unified diff at approval
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Render ChangePreview as unified hunks: file header, @@ ranges, context, additions, removals.
  • Reuse niucode's Toolbox::preview result; niuse copies no path policy and performs no extra reads.
  • Cap the rendered diff at 80 lines with an explicit "more line(s)" marker.
  • Keep the approval prompt below the diff; non-TTY still falls back to a line reply.

Acceptance

  • Write / edit approval shows real hunks with + and - lines.
  • A new file is marked as new; command and note previews still render.
  • Long previews are capped instead of flooding the terminal.
  • Rendering has unit tests; the security boundary is unchanged.

Notes

This was the last known gap between niuse's approval prompt and niucode's TUI preview.

cards.title: Memory recall across expired entries
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem search <query> [--fresh] searches every saved memory, including expired ones.
  • /mem recall <query> does the same inside the REPL.
  • Ranking prefers substring and tag matches over character-bigram similarity, which is weak for short queries.
  • Results show age, expiry state, tags, and the entry id.

Acceptance

  • Expired entries are searchable but still excluded from injection.
  • --fresh hides expired entries.
  • Substring and tag matches outrank unrelated entries; threshold is 0.2.
  • Core scoring has unit tests; CLI and REPL paths were exercised manually.

Notes

Recall is the reason expired memory is kept instead of deleted: it leaves the prompt, not the store.

cards.title: Acceptance metrics and stats
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • ~/.niuse/metrics.jsonl: tab-separated local counters, file 0600.
  • Record turn outcomes, candidate proposals and decisions, journal writes, loops, manual memories, and bootstrap review decisions.
  • niuse stats [--days N] and /stats summarise the window; --days 0 means all time.
  • Acceptance rate is accepted over proposed; edited and replace/keep decisions count as accepted.

Acceptance

  • Metrics append atomically and stay 0600.
  • Parsing and summarisation have unit tests, including a window filter.
  • The CLI and REPL expose the summary.
  • No memory text is written to the metrics file.

Notes

exec turns are counted in the same turn series. Candidates printed by exec are not counted as proposals, because no decision is collected.

This is the measurement M2-001 needs: without it, "acceptance rate ≥ 60%" is a feeling. The file is local-only and excluded from injection.

cards.title: Doctor health check
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse doctor and /doctor check the home directory and mode, identity, user profile, memory counts, thread readability, metrics, credentials, bwrap, and the niucode pin.
  • Offline: no model call, no network.
  • Failures return a non-zero exit; warnings do not.
  • The pin check only runs inside a checkout where niucode.rev exists.

Acceptance

  • A healthy store reports zero failures.
  • Missing credentials are a failure; missing identity or bwrap is a warning.
  • A drifted sibling checkout is reported with the sync command.
  • Report counters have a unit test.

Notes

Doctor is the onboarding answer to "why will it not run": one command, explicit levels, and the exact next step.

cards.title: Manual loops
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse loops add <text> [--due YYYY-MM-DD] creates a promise without waiting for the model to emit a block.
  • /loop <text> does the same inside the REPL.
  • Due dates are validated; invalid dates are rejected before anything is written.
  • Secret scanning applies to manual loops too.
  • Creation is recorded in metrics.

Acceptance

  • A manual loop persists with an optional due date.
  • An invalid due date writes nothing and exits non-zero.
  • The REPL path records the loop and a metric.
  • The CLI listing shows open and overdue entries.

Notes

The model is not the only source of promises. This closes the gap where you know something needs tracking but the turn did not produce a loop block.

cards.title: Memory maintenance: show and edit
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem show <id> prints kind, tags, created, confirmed, source, and text.
  • niuse mem edit <id> opens the text in $EDITOR, normalises it to one line, rescans for secrets, and refreshes the confirmation date.
  • /mem show <id> works in the REPL; candidate editing reuses the same editor helper.
  • IDs accept m-, l-, or no prefix.

Acceptance

  • Show prints every field a reviewer needs.
  • Edit updates the text and confirmed date, or reports no change.
  • A secret in the edited text is refused and the stored entry is untouched.
  • The editor helper is shared with candidate editing; ID prefixes have a test.

Notes

Correcting a wrong memory is as important as adding one: a bad entry is injected on every turn until it is fixed.

cards.title: Journal search
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse journal --search <query> ranks journal bullets across all months.
  • /journal search <query> does the same in the REPL.
  • Ranking reuses the memory scorer: substring hits first, bigram similarity above 0.2.
  • Results show the date and the bullet, capped at ten.

Acceptance

  • A substring hit is found and keeps its date.
  • An unrelated query returns no rows.
  • The CLI and REPL paths were exercised.
  • Ranking and empty-result behaviour have unit tests.

Notes

Memory answers "what is true"; the journal answers "when did we decide this". Search is what makes the second question cheap.

cards.title: Markdown export
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse export [--out FILE] [--session PATH] projects a session log to Markdown.
  • User and assistant turns keep their order; tool calls and results are fenced.
  • Protocol blocks are stripped, exactly as the REPL strips them.
  • Tool output is clipped at 4,000 characters; exported files are 0600.

Acceptance

  • Turns render in order with a metadata header.
  • Protocol blocks never leak into the export.
  • Long tool output is clipped with a marker.
  • Writes to --out are private; stdout works without a file.
  • Unit tests cover ordering, clipping, and block stripping.

Notes

The event log remains the source of truth. The export is a read-only projection for review, backup, or attaching a transcript to an issue.

cards.title: Config file defaults
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • ~/.niuse/config.toml with a [defaults] table: provider, model, sandbox, approval, network, max_steps.
  • Precedence is CLI flag → config file → built-in default.
  • niuse config init writes a commented template; config show prints the file.
  • Settings resolve lazily: offline commands (mem, loops, journal, export, status, stats) do not read the config, so a broken file cannot block them.
  • Config files are 0600.

Acceptance

  • TOML parsing and the precedence rule have unit tests.
  • A config sandbox changes the REPL banner; a CLI flag overrides it.
  • A malformed config fails agent commands with the file path, but status still works.
  • Init refuses to overwrite without --force.

Notes

Defaults belong in a file, not in muscle memory. Lazy resolution is deliberate: a typo in config.toml should not make niuse mem show unusable.

cards.title: Manual journal entries and identity editing
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse journal --add <text> and /journal add <text> append a bullet to today.
  • niuse identity show|edit and /identity edit open the identity file in $EDITOR.
  • Journal entries are secret-scanned and recorded in metrics.
  • Editing uses a multiline helper; memory and candidate editing keep the one-line normaliser.

Acceptance

  • A manual journal entry appears in recent_journal and in search.
  • Identity editing writes the file and keeps it 0600.
  • Empty edits report "no change" and do not write.
  • The journal path has a unit test; identity editing was exercised with a scripted editor.

Notes

Not every durable line comes from the model. Manual entry is the escape hatch when a block was not emitted.

cards.title: Bootstrap inbox merge
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Re-running niuse bootstrap merges into the existing queue instead of replacing it.
  • Pending entries that have since been accepted into memory are dropped.
  • Secret-bearing entries are dropped from both sides.
  • New candidates are deduplicated against memory, the existing queue, and each other.

Acceptance

  • Pending entries survive a second run; accepted ones disappear.
  • Duplicate candidates are not queued twice.
  • The merge rule has a unit test.
  • The CLI reports new versus total pending.

Notes

Cold start is not a one-shot operation: sessions accumulate, and a second mining pass should add to the queue, not erase it.

cards.title: Thread rotation
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /new appends a session end, archives the current thread to ~/.niuse/threads/thread-<millis>.jsonl, and opens a fresh default thread.
  • --thread PATH resumes an archived thread without changing the default.
  • The archive keeps the original JSONL untouched; history comes from the normal projection.
  • /status reports the active thread, not the default path.

Acceptance

  • /new archives the old file and creates a fresh three-event session.
  • --thread resumes an archive and reports its event count.
  • A missing archive source is a no-op.
  • Archive moves have unit tests.

Notes

The default remains one continuous relationship. /new is a chapter break, not the normal path; old chapters stay readable and resumable.

cards.title: Piped output exits cleanly
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse ... | head no longer panics when the reader closes early; the process exits 0.
  • Only the "Broken pipe" panic is intercepted; every other panic goes to the default hook unchanged.
  • The fix is a panic hook rather than a global SIGPIPE reset, because SIGPIPE also covers socket writes made by the provider.

Acceptance

  • niuse mem list | head -1 exits 0 with no panic output.
  • niuse status | head -1 behaves the same.
  • Non-pipe panics still print through the default hook.
  • niuse status --thread <archive> reports the requested thread.

Notes

Small, but it was the first papercut hit while testing; a CLI that panics when paged is not pleasant to script against.

cards.title: Thread listing
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse threads lists the active thread and every archive under ~/.niuse/threads/.
  • Each row shows age, event count, size, and the path relative to the niuse home.
  • The active thread is marked with *, respecting --thread.
  • Invalid sessions still appear with an event count of zero rather than hiding.

Acceptance

  • The active thread and one archive are both listed.
  • The active marker follows --thread / the default path.
  • Age and size formatting have unit tests.
  • Listing is read-only and does not open sessions for append.

Notes

/new made archives; without a listing they were only discoverable with ls. This closes the loop.

cards.title: Expired memory pruning
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem prune lists entries older than 90 days and changes nothing.
  • niuse mem prune --apply removes exactly those entries and records a metric.
  • Fresh and stale-but-valid entries are untouched.
  • Deletion is explicit; there is no implicit expiry write path.

Acceptance

  • Dry run lists the expired entry and leaves the store unchanged.
  • --apply removes only expired entries; a fresh lesson survives.
  • The removal path has a unit test.
  • The metric records how many entries were pruned.

Notes

Soft expiry means expired entries already leave the prompt. Pruning is housekeeping for the file, not a behaviour change; that is why it is manual.

cards.title: Stats daily trend
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse stats --trend adds a per-day breakdown for the selected window.
  • Days are UTC dates; each row shows turns, accepted/proposed, and acceptance.
  • At most the last fourteen active days are printed.
  • /stats keeps the summary view; the flag is CLI-only for now.

Acceptance

  • Metrics on two UTC days produce two rows.
  • Acceptance is - on days without proposals.
  • Grouping has a unit test with synthetic timestamps.
  • A real metrics file renders without panics.

Notes

The dogfood question is not "what is the total" but "is it getting better"; a daily view makes that visible.

cards.title: Bootstrap dry run
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap --dry-run selects sessions exactly as a real run would, then stops.
  • It prints each session id and the transcript size in characters.
  • No provider request is made, so the preview is free.
  • Empty or tool-only sessions are still filtered before the preview.

Acceptance

  • Dry run lists the selected sessions and their transcript sizes.
  • No model call and no inbox write.
  • The selection path is shared with the real run.
  • The CLI path was exercised with a real session directory.

Notes

Bootstrap can cost a model call per session; a free preview is the difference between "try it" and "avoid it".

cards.title: Manual memory duplicate guard
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem add runs the same similarity rule as candidate writes.
  • A match prints the similar ids and refuses unless --force is passed.
  • --force now overrides both the secret scan and the duplicate check; the help text says so.
  • Candidate and manual writes therefore share one conflict definition.

Acceptance

  • A near-duplicate manual add is refused and lists the existing id.
  • --force adds it and the store grows to two entries.
  • The guard has a unit test.
  • Secret scanning still runs before the duplicate check.

Notes

The confirmation flow already prevented duplicates; the manual path was the hole. Closing it keeps the store reviewable at 50 entries.

cards.title: Dogfood record tooling
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse stats --json emits a stable summary plus per-day rows for scripting.
  • docs/dogfood.md defines the ten-day ritual: one row per day, two numbers, one sentence.
  • The JSON includes turns, candidate decisions, acceptance, activity counts, and days.
  • /stats keeps the human summary; --json is CLI-only.

Acceptance

  • JSON output parses and includes acceptance_percent and days.
  • Serialization has a unit test with synthetic metrics.
  • The dogfood guide links the exact command and a table template.
  • README points at the guide.

Notes

The point of the JSON is not dashboards; it is making the daily row cheap enough to actually write.

cards.title: User profile editing
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse user show|edit and /user / /user edit expose user.md.
  • Editing uses the multiline $EDITOR helper and keeps the file 0600.
  • A missing file opens a small template with the three questions that matter: current work, working style, red lines.
  • The edit is recorded in metrics.

Acceptance

  • Show prints the path and content, or a hint when missing.
  • Edit writes the file through a scripted editor and user show reflects it.
  • Empty edits report no change.
  • Permissions remain 0600.

Notes

identity.md says who it is; user.md says who you are. The second one had no manual path, only bootstrap.

cards.title: Bootstrap profile draft
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap --profile makes one extra model call and drafts user.md from the selected sessions.
  • It only writes when user.md is missing or --force-profile is passed.
  • Input is capped at 10k characters; output is asked for three sections and no speculation.
  • --dry-run reports that a profile would be drafted without calling anything.
  • The write is recorded in metrics.

Acceptance

  • A fresh home gets a user.md draft; an existing one is skipped by default.
  • The input builder respects its cap (unit test).
  • The draft is written 0600 and the command suggests niuse user edit.
  • A real run produced a draft that admitted uncertainty instead of inventing facts.

Notes

This is the missing half of the cold start described in the plan: candidates fill memory, the profile fills user.md. identity.md is still never mined.

cards.title: Secret scan for identity and profile edits
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • identity edit, user edit, and identity init scan the final text before writing.
  • bootstrap --profile refuses a generated draft that contains a secret pattern.
  • A refusal leaves the existing file untouched and exits non-zero.
  • Memory, journal, and loop writes already had the same guard.

Acceptance

  • A scripted editor inserting sk-... is refused for identity and user.
  • The existing identity file is unchanged after the refusal.
  • The profile draft path checks before write_user.
  • The scan uses the same built-in patterns as other writes.

Notes

Identity and user text is injected on every turn; a leaked key there would be sent to the provider continuously. The guard belongs at the write, not only in memory.

cards.title: Profile-only bootstrap
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap --profile-only implies --profile and stops after drafting user.md.
  • It skips the per-session candidate extraction, saving one call per session.
  • The existing inbox is left untouched.
  • --dry-run still previews the sessions and the profile intent without a model call.

Acceptance

  • --profile-only sets the profile path even without --profile.
  • The command returns before candidate extraction.
  • Dry run reports the profile intent and lists sessions.
  • README documents the flag.

Notes

Sometimes only the "who you are" half is missing. Making the user pay for candidate extraction in that case is unnecessary.

cards.title: Machine-readable memory output
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem list --json emits the visible entries as a JSON array.
  • niuse mem search <query> --json emits ranked matches with the same shape.
  • Fields: id, kind, tags, created, confirmed, age_days, expired, source, text.
  • Expiry state is computed at read time; the file format is unchanged.

Acceptance

  • Both commands emit valid JSON that parses.
  • expired and age_days reflect the current date.
  • Serialization has a unit test.
  • Text output is unchanged when the flag is absent.

Notes

Markdown stays the storage format. JSON is an output view for scripts and dogfood, not a second store.

cards.title: Memory kind filter
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem list --kind preference|lesson filters the visible entries.
  • niuse mem search <query> --kind ... applies the same filter before ranking.
  • An unknown kind fails with the two accepted values.
  • --json respects the filter; text output keeps the global counts.

Acceptance

  • Listing lessons hides preferences.
  • Search ranks only the requested kind.
  • An invalid kind exits non-zero with a clear message.
  • Kind parsing has a unit test.

Notes

At fifty entries the list is still readable, but "show me only decisions" is a real review need.

cards.title: JSON for threads and journal
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse threads --json lists archives with a path relative to the niuse home, active flag, events, bytes, and age.
  • niuse journal --json emits day objects; with --search, hit objects with date and text.
  • The text output is unchanged when the flag is absent; --add ignores --json.
  • All three persistent stores now have a machine-readable view alongside Markdown.

Acceptance

  • Threads JSON uses relative paths and marks exactly one active thread.
  • Journal show/search JSON parse and keep dates.
  • Thread conversion has a unit test.
  • Existing text output is untouched.

Notes

Markdown remains the only storage. JSON is a read view for scripts, not a second source of truth.

cards.title: Effective config view
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse config effective prints the merged values: provider, model, sandbox, approval, network, max_steps.
  • Precedence is the same as runtime: CLI flag, then config file, then built-in.
  • max_steps = 0 is shown as unlimited; a missing model is shown as the provider default.
  • No provider or credential is constructed.
  • The doctor hint now points at bootstrap --profile and user edit.

Acceptance

  • Defaults print on a clean home.
  • CLI flags override the file in the printed view.
  • An end-to-end CLI test asserts the override.
  • The command works without network or credentials.

Notes

The raw file answers "what did I configure"; this answers "what will actually run".

cards.title: Doctor JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse doctor --json emits {checks, failures, warnings}.
  • Each check has level (ok / warn / fail), label, and detail.
  • Human output is unchanged when the flag is absent.
  • Exit semantics stay the same: failures are non-zero, warnings are zero.

Acceptance

  • JSON parses and contains every check.
  • Levels serialize in lowercase.
  • The report counters still have a unit test, now also covering serialization.
  • Existing human output is untouched.

Notes

CI and setup scripts can now assert on the same facts a human sees, instead of scraping [ok] prefixes.

cards.title: Status and loops JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse status --json emits nested memory, loops, and prompt sections plus home, thread, identity, and user flags.
  • niuse loops list --json emits id, text, due, done, and overdue.
  • Human output is unchanged when the flag is absent.
  • Both commands are covered by end-to-end CLI tests.

Acceptance

  • Status JSON parses and reports zero-state counts.
  • Loops JSON round-trips a due date.
  • Overdue is computed at read time.
  • Existing text output is untouched.

Notes

This closes the JSON surface: memory, journal, threads, loops, status, doctor, and stats all have a machine-readable view.

cards.title: Release and dependency strategy
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Decide the niucode dependency: publish niucode crates first, pin a git revision, or support cargo install --git only.
  • Add license, repository, description, and other release metadata.
  • Make cargo package / cargo publish --dry-run reproducible.
  • Confirm crate-name availability; rename the crate if needed while keeping the niuse binary.

Acceptance

  • cargo package -p niuse passes (currently blocked by path dependencies).
  • The install path is reproducible on a clean machine.
  • License and naming strategy are documented in the README.

Notes

Findings and options are recorded in distribution.

Current failure: all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging, pointing at the niucode-agent path dependency.

cards.title: Reuse niucode's TUI through a library and hooks
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niucode-cli exposes a library target: session runtime, TUI entry, renderer, approval UI.
  • A small hook surface: augment the system prompt before a turn, observe a finished turn, receive session lifecycle events.
  • niuse implements the hooks: identity / memory injection, candidate extraction, journal and loop writes.
  • Delete niuse's renderer and its per-turn AgentConfig assembly once the shared path is stable.

Acceptance

  • A niuse binary runs niucode's TUI with memory injected and candidates confirmed.
  • niuse no longer owns a renderer or a second terminal input loop.
  • The hook trait is generic: no identity or memory types cross into niucode.
  • Contract tests still pass against the pinned revision.

Notes

This is the only large piece of duplication left. Keeping two repos is still the decision (ADR-0003); this card removes the reason the boundary felt wrong, without merging the products.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: niuse boundaries, the five stores, turn data flow, write thresholds, and explicit non-goals.
docs.body_html:
In one sentence

niuse is the identity and memory layer above niucode: it decides who the companion is, what it remembers, and what it promised. Whether a task can be done at all stays with niucode's loop, tools, and sandbox.

Dependency direction

crates/niuse-cli     REPL / commands / renderer / driver / bootstrap
    │
crates/niuse-core    date / model / store / prompt / candidate / policy
    │
niucode-agent        run_with_history / AgentConfig / project_history
niucode-core         SessionLog / Event
niucode-provider     Provider / ChatMessage
niucode-auth         AuthStore
niucode-tools        SandboxPolicy / ApprovalMode

Only driver.rs touches niucode-agent directly. Everything else is either pure domain logic or only knows niuse-core types. When niucode upgrades, the required changes are confined to one file.

niuse does not fork niucode and does not add a memory hook to its loop. Memory is a product layer; the kernel stays minimal.

Today niuse owns the REPL and renderer. ADR-0003 moves the front end upstream: niucode-cli grows a library target and a generic turn-hook surface, and niuse becomes the product layer that implements it. Until that lands, the renderer stays here deliberately, not accidentally.

Modules

ModuleLayerResponsibility
cliInterfaceflags, subcommands, offline commands, wiring
replInterfaceconversation, slash commands, candidate confirmation, rendering
promptEnginestable-prefix system prompt and budgets
protocolEnginein-band block parsing and streaming stripping
policyEnginesoft expiry, conflicts, secret scanning
driverAdaptersniucode boundary, sessions, per-turn cwd
bootstrapAdaptersold-session mining and the inbox
storesStatefive-store load / save and permissions
dashboardEngineeringoffline board generation

Turn data flow

startup
  ├─ read identity / user / memory / loops / journal
  ├─ compose() assembles the system prompt (once per session)
  └─ project_history(thread.jsonl) restores history

user input
  ├─ run_with_history(config, prompt, history)
  ├─ AgentEvent → Renderer (TextDelta goes through StreamFilter)
  ├─ trailing buffer strips <<niuse:*>> blocks
  ├─ journal / loop: written automatically
  ├─ memory: print candidate → y / n / e / s
  └─ re-project history, next turn

There is no second copy of the conversation. niuse export renders the event log as Markdown without changing it. history is projected from the event log by niucode's project_history, so compaction, replay, and fork behave exactly as they do in niucode.

The five stores and injection

~/.niuse/
  identity.md      who it is (human-written; it may only propose)
  user.md          who you are (bootstrapped with --profile, human-reviewed)
  memory/          facts: preferences, decisions, pitfalls (confirmed, expiring)
  journal/         experience: one file per month, merged per day (automatic)
  loops.md         promises (automatic, optional due date)
  thread.jsonl     the relationship thread
  threads/         archived chapters from `/new`
  inbox.md         bootstrap review queue

Defaults come from CLI flags, then ~/.niuse/config.toml, then built-ins; only commands that build a provider read the file.

Injection order is fixed, stable before volatile:

SectionBudgetChange rate
personaconstantnever
identity≤ 600 tokvery low
user≤ 600 toklow
memory≤ 2 000 toklow
protocolconstantnever
todayone linedaily
loops≤ 300 tokmedium
journal≤ 600 tokhigh

The first five sections form the stable cache prefix; only content after today can vary per session. The system prompt is assembled once and is not rebuilt mid-session.

Write thresholds and protocol

WhatWho decidesConfirmation
journal, loopsthe companionnone
memoryit proposesrequired
identitythe humanonly the human can change it

The model may end an answer with three block types:

<<niuse:memory kind=preference tags=rust,testing>>
one self-contained conclusion
<</niuse:memory>>

<<niuse:loop due=2026-10-22>>
something it promised to do
<</niuse:loop>>

<<niuse:journal>>
- a decision or turning point that differs from last time
<</niuse:journal>>

At most one memory block per turn; after a rejection, the same tags are not proposed again in that session. journal records changes, not activity logs. Expired memory leaves the prompt but stays searchable through niuse mem search and /mem recall.

Safety and privacy

  • ~/.niuse directories are 0700, files are 0600; writes go to a temporary file and are renamed.
  • Secret patterns are scanned before every write; a match is refused, and the CLI requires --force to override where an override exists.
  • identity.md and user.md edits, and the bootstrap profile draft, are refused on a secret match; these files are injected every turn.
  • Manual mem add runs the same conflict rule as candidates; --force overrides both the secret and duplicate checks.
  • Approval renders niucode's structured change preview (hunks, capped at 80 lines) before asking.
  • Memory is sent to the provider on every turn, so the leak surface is larger than a normal file.
  • Project knowledge stays in the repo's AGENTS.md; niuse never edits your repositories.
  • NIUSE_MEMORY=off disables injection and candidates, for A/B runs and for recovering trust.
  • niuse doctor checks home permissions, identity, credentials, bwrap, and the pinned niucode revision without calling a model.
  • metrics.jsonl records local counters only: turn outcomes, candidate decisions, tags, and ids. Memory text never enters it.

Explicit non-goals

A daemon, a web UI, WeChat / Feishu bridges, scheduled push notifications, vector search, full session indexing, automatic repo edits, multi-user support, a TUI (for now), or a general agent framework.

There is one test for every proposal: does this shape an identity, or is it just another capability?

docs.title: Implementation plan
docs.summary: Fifteen decisions, the five stores, turn lifecycle, write thresholds, milestones, and verifiable acceptance.
docs.body_html:
In one sentence

Add a persistent identity and memory layer above niucode so the same agent knows you across projects and sessions. No resident service, no vector search, no automatic edits to your repositories.

1. Positioning

niucode owns "can do": loop, tools, sandbox, event log. niuse owns "who": what it remembers, what it promised, and when it should disagree with you.

One test decides whether a feature belongs here: does it shape an identity, or is it just another capability? Capabilities stay in niucode or are not built.

2. Decisions

#QuestionDecision
D1PositioningCross-project engineering memory
D2ContentPreferences, decisions, pitfalls; few, high-value, reviewable
D3OwnershipGlobal preferences in niuse; project knowledge in the repo's AGENTS.md
D4WritingThe agent proposes, one key confirms; at most one per turn
D5ReadingFull injection filtered by scope
D6ArchitectureSeparate repo, depends on niucode libs, drives turns itself
D7Storage~/.niuse/, plain Markdown, 0600
D8InterfaceInteractive REPL; TUI deferred
D9ExpirySoft expiry, replace on conflict
D10PrivacySecret-pattern blacklist, refuse on match
D11MVPOnly the global-preference loop
D12Top riskConfirmation fatigue
D13ShapeIdentity layer plus resumable session, no resident process
D14Cold startMine history; you define identity
D15CharacterAn opinionated collaborator

Rationale for each trade-off lives in ADR-0001 and ADR-0002.

Admission criteria for memory

A piece of information may enter memory/ only if all three hold:

  1. It is still useful across sessions.
  2. It cannot be found by grep in the repository.
  3. It fits in one sentence a human can review.

Anything else is rejected. This is what keeps "index every session" and "environment facts" out: they look like memory but are really retrieval and configuration.

3. Stores and injection

3.1 The five stores

~/.niuse/
  identity.md          who it is: name, voice, values, boundaries
  user.md              who you are: goals, rhythm, taste, red lines, current work
  memory/
    preferences.md
    lessons.md         decisions and pitfalls
  journal/
    2026-10.md         experience, one file per month
  loops.md             promises: things it said it would do
  • UTF-8 Markdown only; directories 0700, files 0600.
  • memory/ may be its own git repository for backup and diffs; journal/ is not committed by default.
  • No database. For a single user and under 200 entries, files are the best query engine.

3.2 Injection order and budget

Stable before volatile; the system prompt is assembled once per session (never rebuilt mid-session, to avoid a cache miss on every turn):

SectionSourceBudgetChange rate
Identityidentity.md≤ 600 tokvery low
Useruser.md≤ 600 toklow
Factsmemory/*.md≤ 2 000 toklow
Promisesloops.md≤ 300 tokmedium
Recent experiencelast 3 journal/ days≤ 600 tokhigh

About 4k tokens in total. Over budget, drop the oldest unverified facts first, then truncate the journal; never silently drop identity or user.

3.3 Entry format

One memory is one section: machine-parseable and human-readable.

### m-7f3a

- Conclusion: Rust repositories use `cargo nextest`, never `cargo test`
- Tags: rust, testing
- Created: 2026-10-21
- Last confirmed: 2026-10-21
- Source: `1792493790852-350850-0`

id is four random hex digits and is never reused. Source points at the niucode session id and is the only audit trail.

loops.md:

- [ ] l-7f3a Confirm whether niucode supports per-turn cwd (due 2026-10-22)
- [x] l-91cc Cap the bootstrap sample (2026-10-21)

4. Turn lifecycle

startup
  ├─ read the five stores
  ├─ assemble the system prompt (once)
  └─ restore thread history via project_history

each input
  ├─ run_with_history(config, prompt, history)
  ├─ stream events (own renderer)
  ├─ tail buffer: strip <<niuse:memory>> / <<niuse:loop>> / <<niuse:journal>> blocks
  ├─ candidate? print it → y / n / e
  ├─ accept → write memory (or loops)
  └─ append to the journal buffer

exit / project switch
  └─ journal is already on disk

history is projected by niucode's project_history from session events; there is no second copy of the conversation. Replay, fork, and compaction therefore behave exactly as in niucode, and niuse does not reinvent them.

5. Write thresholds

5.1 Candidate protocol

No extra model call. The system prompt states that the model may append a block when a turn produced something durable:

<<niuse:memory kind=preference tags=rust,testing>>
Rust repositories use cargo nextest, never cargo test
<</niuse:memory>>

Rules:

  • At most one block per turn; if there is nothing, say nothing. Long runs without a candidate are normal.
  • Only memory and loop and journal blocks are recognised.
  • After a memory rejection, the same tags are not proposed again in that session.
  • A parse failure counts as "no candidate": no error, no guessing.

The cost is that the model may miss things. Missing is acceptable; recording something wrong is not — the same value as D9. If dogfooding shows serious under-recording after two weeks, add an offline proposer then, not now.

5.2 Confirmation

Memory candidate [global · rust,testing]
  Rust repositories use cargo nextest, never cargo test
  [y] accept   [n] discard   [e] edit   [s] stop proposing this session

e opens $EDITOR. A conflict does not overwrite silently:

Conflicts with m-91cc:
  old: Rust projects use cargo test
  new: Rust repositories use cargo nextest
  [r] replace   [k] keep both   [d] discard

5.3 Journal

Written automatically, no confirmation, but only under strict rules:

  • Three to five lines, only what differs from last time: decisions, turning points, open questions, mood shifts.
  • No activity logs ("fixed a bug today"), no duplication of memory/.
  • Events and judgements only, not code detail. Paths may be referenced; code is not copied.
  • Scanned for secrets before writing, since transcripts may contain keys.

The journal is not a log; it is compressed shared experience. The test: read it three months later and see whether the trade-off comes back.

5.4 Loops

  • When it says "I'll check next time" or "I'll follow up", that goes into loops.md; otherwise trust erodes.
  • Each entry may carry a due date; entries without one surface after two weeks.
  • Closing a loop needs evidence (a verification, a conclusion), not a feeling of completion.

6. Expiry, conflicts, privacy

6.1 Soft expiry

Age since last confirmedInjection behaviour
≤ 30 daysinjected normally
31–90 daysinjected, marked (unverified since YYYY-MM-DD)
> 90 daysnot injected automatically; visible via /mem recall

No automatic deletion. Deletion is irreversible and you would never know what it removed. /mem review supports bulk re-confirmation and cleanup.

journal is exempt from expiry: experience does not become invalid, only old. loops uses due dates, not age.

6.2 Conflicts

Before writing, a new memory is compared with the existing store:

  • normalise (lowercase, strip punctuation), take character bigrams, Jaccard ≥ 0.5 is a likely conflict;
  • same tag and similarity ≥ 0.35 also counts;
  • a hit opens replace / keep both / discard; never merge automatically.

The 0.5 threshold is a starting point and will be adjusted after two weeks of false positives. No embeddings: at 200 entries the complexity outweighs the benefit.

6.3 Privacy

Memory is sent to the provider every turn, so leaked content leaks far more often than in an ordinary file. Every write is scanned; a hit is refused with a reason:

PatternExample
sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}OpenAI / DeepSeek key
ghp_ / github_pat_GitHub token
AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}AWS access key
-----BEGIN .* PRIVATE KEY-----private key
xox[baprs]-Slack token
32+ hex / base64 rungeneric key shape

Scanning is a backstop, not a guarantee. Private projects, client names, and internal addresses still depend on human judgement at confirmation time. NIUSE_MEMORY=off disables injection entirely, for A/B runs and trust recovery.

7. Cold start

niuse bootstrap turns history into user.md and memory candidates once:

  1. Enumerate ~/.niucode/sessions/*.jsonl, last 90 days, at most 40; prefer sessions with multiple turns and tool calls.
  2. Send only user / assistant text, dropping tool output, through one tool-free extraction that returns {type, text, evidence}.
  3. Deduplicate, group by type, and write ~/.niuse/inbox.md with the source session id on every line.
  4. niuse review walks the queue: y accept, n discard, e edit.
  5. With --profile, one extra call drafts user.md from the same sessions when the file is missing; --force-profile overwrites.
  6. identity.md is not mined: niuse identity init asks eight questions, records your answers, and lets you edit them.

Cost estimate: 40 sessions × about 2k input tokens ≈ 100k tokens, one-off.

Mining boundary: only the three kinds from D2. No code facts, no environment configuration, no information about other people.

8. Architecture

crates/niuse-cli     REPL, commands, renderer, driver, bootstrap
    │
crates/niuse-core    date / model / store / prompt / candidate / policy
    │
niucode-agent        run_with_history / AgentConfig / project_history
niucode-core         SessionLog / Event
niucode-provider / auth / tools
  • Two crates: niuse-core depends only on anyhow and regex, and its 38 tests need no API key; niuse-cli owns the terminal, provider wiring, and driver.
  • The dependency currently points at a sibling checkout via a path. Publishing or moving machines requires a pinned git revision instead.
  • A NiucodeDriver-style seam (about 200 lines) isolates API churn: config assembly, history projection, event forwarding.
  • niucode-cli is a binary with no library target, so the MVP does not reuse its TUI or renderer. It writes a minimal renderer and can swap later once upstream exposes a library or a hook.
  • No changes to niucode's loop, no memory hook in the kernel. Memory is a product layer; the kernel stays minimal.

9. Three assumptions verified in W1

Written down is not verified. Each was tested in the first week; if any had failed, the design would have changed.

  1. Per-turn cwd on one session — passes: reading in one directory, /cd /tmp, reading in another, both succeed in the same thread.jsonl, with history rebuilt correctly.
  2. Reliable stripping of trailing candidate blocks in a stream — passes: the filter covers blocks split across chunks, partial prefixes, false markers, and unterminated blocks; real calls show the block removed and the prose intact.
  3. niucode-agent's public API fits a thin adapter — passes: driver.rs is about 200 lines with nothing to fork or bypass. The only thing written from scratch is the renderer, because niucode-cli has no library target.

10. Milestones

WeekDeliverableStatus
W1Three spikes; crate skeleton; five-store reads/writes; prompt assembly; one real turn in the REPLdone
W2Candidate block and confirmation; journal; loops; soft expiry; secret scandone (approval preview is still a summary, not a full diff)
W3niuse bootstrap; dogfood; acceptance databootstrap and review done; dogfood pending

11. Acceptance

Technical checks passed on 2026-10-21: five-store reads/writes and 0600, candidate protocol, streaming strip, soft expiry, secret scan, the full bootstrap → review → memory chain, per-turn cwd in one session, and cargo xtask dashboard --check.

What remains is product acceptance, which requires real use:

  • Ten consecutive working days, at least one real task per day through niuse
  • Candidate acceptance rate ≥ 60% (accepted / proposed)
  • At least 3 cases where it cites a past judgement and the citation is correct
  • At least 1 case where it disagrees and you change your mind
  • Memory store ≤ 50 entries (more means the bar is too low)
  • At least 1 A/B case where NIUSE_MEMORY=off produces a different answer

The last item is the anti-placebo check: if turning memory off changes nothing, the layer has no reason to exist.

12. Non-goals

Daemon, web UI, WeChat / Feishu bridges, scheduled push, vector search, full session indexing, automatic repo edits, multi-user support, a TUI (for now), a general agent framework.

13. Risks

RiskSymptomMitigation
Confirmation fatigue (top)Blind y presses, then the feature is switched offAt most one per turn; no repeated tags after rejection; observable acceptance rate; NIUSE_MEMORY=off
Persona performanceLines like "I missed you"Hard rules in identity.md; companionship rests on memory, promises, disagreement
Journal becomes an activity log"Fixed a bug today"Only changes and judgements; monthly review removes empty entries
Dependency rotniucode moves and the build breaksPin the revision; thin adapter; upstream a library split if needed
Cold-start noise"User likes clean code" × 20Only three kinds; every candidate carries a source; batch review, not accept-all

14. Open questions

  • Its name: niuse is the project name, not necessarily what you call it; define that in identity.md.
  • Bootstrap sample size and cost: decide after one real run.
  • Whether it may propose changes to identity.md: proposal yes, confirmation required.
  • Session model beyond a single thread: /new, per-project sessions; wait for real usage to expose the need.

15. Implementation map and deviations

Implemented in crates/niuse-core and crates/niuse-cli:

Plan itemLocation
Five stores, 0600store.rs, atomic write plus chmod
Injection and budgetsprompt.rs, stable sections first
Protocol blocks and streaming stripcandidate.rs, six boundary tests
Soft expiry / conflicts / secret scanpolicy.rs plus prompt.rs
REPL, confirmation, /mem and friendsrepl.rs, commands.rs
Session resume and per-turn cwddriver.rs
Cold startbootstrap.rs (bootstrap + review)
Architecture dashboardcrates/xtask plus docs/dashboard/project.json
Memory kill switchNIUSE_MEMORY=off in repl.rs

Three deviations from the plan:

  1. A third protocol block, journal. The plan had memory and loop only; to avoid an extra model call, the main model emits a journal block and niuse writes it automatically.
  2. exec never writes memory. It prints candidates to stderr so scripted calls cannot change the store silently.
  3. Approval shows a summary and +/- counts. A structured unified diff is deferred; the security boundary is unchanged.

docs.title: ADR-0001: A global memory layer
docs.summary: Memory is a small global store, not a session index: plain Markdown, full injection, soft expiry, confirmation before writing; project knowledge stays in AGENTS.md.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-21. The W1 spike passed; the MVP is implemented in crates/niuse-core (store, policy, prompt, candidate).

Context

niucode already has AGENTS.md, skills, session resume, compaction, and fork, but it deliberately does not provide memory across sessions or projects (the roadmap lists it as deferred). The result: every new project starts by repeating preferences, decisions, and old pitfalls.

The obvious temptation is to index every session and retrieve from it. That direction has three concrete problems:

  1. Code facts are one grep away; indexing duplicates the repository.
  2. Retrieval quality needs an evaluation set, and niuse does not have one.
  3. Vectorising turns "reviewable" into "opaque": a wrong memory cannot be spotted at a glance.

Decision

  1. Memory is global, not per-session. It stores only what still holds across projects; project-level knowledge stays in the repository's AGENTS.md, and niuse never writes there automatically.
  2. Three kinds only: preferences, decisions, pitfalls. Admission requires: useful across sessions, not greppable in the repo, expressible in one reviewable sentence.
  3. Plain Markdown, under ~/.niuse/memory/, files 0600, optionally its own git repo. No SQLite, no JSONL.
  4. Full injection, filtered by scope, 2k-token budget. No query-time retrieval, so the system-prompt prefix stays stable and prompt caching survives.
  5. Confirmation before writing, at most one candidate per turn. The candidate is emitted in-band by the main model; no extra model call.
  6. Soft expiry: normal within 30 days, marked unverified from 31 to 90 days, not injected after 90. Never deleted automatically.
  7. Conflicts are never merged silently: lexical similarity above threshold offers replace / keep both / discard.
  8. Secret-pattern scan before writing; a match is refused. Memory is sent to the provider every turn, so the leak surface is much larger than an ordinary file.

Consequences

Better:

  • Memory is readable, editable, diffable, and revertible; mistakes are visible and fixable.
  • No retrieval dependency, works offline, no embedding service or evaluation set required.
  • The stable prompt prefix preserves the prompt-cache behaviour niucode relies on.

Worse:

  • A hard capacity limit around 200 entries; beyond that, manual merging or pruning is required.
  • Recall is "inject everything and let the model judge"; no relevance ranking, and too much memory dilutes attention.
  • Candidates depend on the main model volunteering them; missing one is normal.

Accepted trade-off: prefer missing a memory to recording a wrong one. A wrong memory enters every subsequent turn and is hard to notice; a missing one costs at most one repeated mistake.

Alternatives

OptionRejected because
Vector index over all sessionsNo evaluation set, not reviewable, duplicates grep, breaks the stable prefix
SQLite storageNo benefit at single-user, 200-entry scale; unreadable to humans and to diffs
Automatic distillationNoisy, and a wrong memory pollutes a turn before anyone can catch it; conflicts with "prefer missing"
Project memory in the global storeDuplicates AGENTS.md and drifts away from the code
Build it into the niucode kernelViolates niucode's minimal-harness boundary; memory should be a replaceable product layer
docs.excerpt: Memory is a small global store, not a session index: plain Markdown, full injection, soft expiry, confirmation before writing; project knowledge stays in AGENTS.md.

docs.title: ADR-0002: An identity layer, not a daemon
docs.summary: Identity is five Markdown stores, not prompt magic; companionship comes from memory, promises, and disagreement, not tone; what persists is the identity, not a process.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-21. The identity layer and REPL are implemented; journal and loops are written automatically from in-band protocol blocks.

Context

The goal is a personal companion, not a smarter tool. Two shapes exist in the ecosystem:

  • pi-memory style: IDENTITY.md / USER.md / MEMORY.md / daily/, injected at session start. Lightweight, but only a memory extension.
  • pi-durable-assistant style: a resident runtime, web UI, scheduled tasks, background subagents, a WeChat channel, and approval-gated memory. Heavy, and it turns a personal project into an operations project.

The cheap way to fake a companion is to give it a persona and a warm tone. That slides quickly into role-play: it talks a lot, remembers little, never disagrees, and does not improve your judgement.

Decision

  1. Identity is files, not prompt magic. identity.md, user.md, memory/, journal/, and loops.md are five persistent stores, all human-readable and editable. You can rewrite its values without touching code.
  2. You write the identity; it may only propose changes. History can mine user.md and memory candidates, but it cannot mine who it is.
  3. Injection order is stable-to-volatile: identity → user → memory → loops → recent journal. The system prompt is assembled once per session.
  4. Graded write thresholds: journal and loops are automatic; memory requires confirmation; identity is human-only.
  5. No daemon. No web UI, no WeChat, no scheduled push. It exists while the terminal is open and does not pretend to live in the background.
  6. Companionship rests on three things: remembering your judgements, tracking its own promises, and speaking up when you are wrong. Not emotional performance, not pet names, not spontaneous sentiment.
  7. It keeps a right to disagree. identity.md must state its judgement criteria and boundaries; disagreement comes with reasons, about the work rather than the person.
  8. The journal records change only. Three to five lines covering decisions, turning points, open questions, and shifts in mood; no activity logs, no duplication of memory.

Consequences

Better:

  • The identity is fully auditable: one git diff shows what changed about its character.
  • No operational burden: no servers, ports, certificates, or backup strategy.
  • Cold start can borrow history, so the first two weeks do not feel like meeting a stranger.

Worse:

  • It only exists while the terminal is open; it cannot remind you on a commute.
  • Without push, the freshness of loops depends on you opening the terminal.
  • Identity quality depends on whether you answer the eight questions; skip them and it degrades into a generic assistant.

Accepted trade-off: prove that "remembers, reliable, willing to disagree" is valuable before adding reach. Doing it the other way around produces a role-playing bot that interrupts you everywhere.

Alternatives

OptionRejected because
Resident daemon plus pushAbout five times the work, and it turns a personal project into an operations project; reach can come later
A persona paragraph in the system promptNot auditable, not revertible, and it drifts on every startup
Let the model self-update its identityIt slowly drifts toward pleasing you, which destroys the willingness to disagree
Reuse pi-durable-assistantA complete Node + SQLite runtime, incompatible with "built on niucode"
Rebuild the persona from memory each sessionNo shared history, nowhere for the journal to accumulate, no relationship to grow
docs.excerpt: Identity is five Markdown stores, not prompt magic; companionship comes from memory, promises, and disagreement, not tone; what persists is the identity, not a process.

docs.title: ADR-0003: niucode is the kernel and UI; niuse is the product
docs.summary: Keep two repositories. Upstream a reusable CLI library and turn hooks; niuse owns identity, memory, policy, and product defaults. Merge only if the product layer becomes thin enough that separate releases stop mattering.
docs.body_html:
Status

Accepted · 2026-10-21.

Upstream proposal: niucode ADR-0032 · niuverse/niucode#1.

Context

niuse currently drives niucode's turn loop itself and owns a small renderer, because niucode-cli is a binary with no library target. Reusing niucode's TUI would remove the duplicate front end, which raises the obvious question: if niuse reuses the TUI, why not merge it into niucode?

Two facts make the merge tempting:

  • The shared surface is large: loop, session, tools, renderer, approval UI, diff preview.
  • Every shared change currently costs a revision bump and a contract test.

Two facts push the other way:

  • niucode's positioning is a minimal, observable coding harness that deliberately refuses long-term memory, resident services, and product defaults. Merging a companion into that repo changes what niucode is.
  • The two projects have different release cadences and different failure modes: kernel breakage versus product annoyance.

Decision

  1. Keep two repositories. niucode is the kernel and the reference UI; niuse is the product layer and the identity.
  2. Move the front end upstream, not the product. niucode-cli should expose a reusable library (TUI, runtime entry) plus a small turn-hook surface:
    • augment the system prompt before a turn;
    • observe a finished turn (for candidate extraction);
    • receive session lifecycle events. niuse implements the hooks and deletes its own renderer once the shared TUI is usable.
  3. Keep the product in niuse: identity, user model, memory, journal, loops, protocol blocks, expiry/conflict/privacy policy, product defaults (model, permissions, persona).
  4. Pin what you consume. niucode.rev fixes the revision required CI and deployments build against. The pin moves at most weekly through scripts/sync-niucode.sh; a nightly job tests niucode main so drift is visible early.
  5. Upstream first. Any capability that a generic niucode user would want lands in niucode first. niuse never forks kernel files.
  6. Set a merge trigger instead of debating forever. After the library split lands, if niuse's product-only surface falls below roughly 1,000 lines and separate releases stop mattering, merging becomes reasonable. Until then, two repos buy a clean kernel story and independent cadence.

Consequences

Better:

  • Reusing the TUI removes the largest duplication without diluting niucode's positioning.
  • The contract test plus pinned revision turns "did upstream break us?" into a CI signal.
  • Product decisions and kernel decisions keep separate ADR trails and release notes.

Worse:

  • niucode must grow a library API and hooks, which is real design work and must stay generic.
  • niuse still carries a binary, product defaults, and the hook implementation.
  • The weekly bump is a recurring chore, even if a small one.

Accepted trade-off: a little ceremony now beats either a fork or a premature monorepo. If the ceremony stops paying for itself, the merge trigger is explicit.

Alternatives

OptionRejected because
Merge niuse into niucode nowChanges what niucode is, couples releases, and mixes two boards and two audiences before the boundary is settled
Add --profile personal to niucodeHides a product inside the kernel; the personal layer would inherit kernel release pressure and vice versa
Fork niucode inside niuseDuplicates the loop and the front end, and guarantees drift
Keep the duplicate renderer foreverCheapest this month, most expensive this year; every TUI improvement has to be rebuilt twice
docs.excerpt: Keep two repositories. Upstream a reusable CLI library and turn hooks; niuse owns identity, memory, policy, and product defaults. Merge only if the product layer becomes thin enough that separate releases stop mattering.

docs.title: niucode compatibility
docs.summary: Pinned niucode revision, the weekly bump ritual, and the nightly check against main.
docs.body_html:
Policy

  • niuse pins niucode in niucode.rev; required CI and Pages check out exactly that commit.
  • The pin moves at most once a week, through scripts/sync-niucode.sh.
  • A nightly workflow runs the same tests against niucode main. Failures are an early signal, not a pull-request gate.
  • scripts/check-niucode-drift.sh reports when the local sibling checkout no longer matches the pin.

The front-end seam is proposed upstream in ADR-0032; this document tracks the call surface niuse uses today.

The contract is deliberately small: run_with_history, AgentConfig, project_history, SessionLog and Event, the provider trait, credentials, sandbox and approval types, per-turn working_dir on one session, and approval denial carrying a structured preview. crates/niuse-cli/tests/niucode_contract.rs exercises them offline with ScriptedProvider, so the check costs no tokens.

Matrix

niuseniucodestatusupdated
0.1.06fd40cacurrent pin; contract tests pass2026-10-22
0.1.095f5303previous pin; contract tests pass2026-10-21
0.1.0b5f66baprevious pin; contract tests pass2026-10-21

Weekly ritual

./scripts/sync-niucode.sh <rev>   # writes niucode.rev, runs tests + dashboard check
cargo xtask dashboard             # refresh the board
# update the matrix above, commit niucode.rev and the generated board

If the nightly job is red, read the contract test failure first. A break there usually means one of two things: an API niuse uses changed shape, or the behaviour behind it changed. Fix upstream when the change is generic; adapt niuse when it is product-specific.

docs.title: Dogfood log
docs.summary: Ten-day protocol: one row per day, numbers from stats --json, plus one concrete memory win or disagreement.
docs.body_html:
Why

M2-001 is a product acceptance gate, not a coding task. It needs ten days of real use, recorded while the context is fresh. The record is deliberately small: one row per day, two numbers, one sentence.

Daily ritual (two minutes)

niuse stats --days 1 --json

Append one row below. proposed / accepted come from the JSON; note is a concrete memory win, a disagreement, or -. Do not reconstruct a missed day later; a gap is honest data.

dateturnsproposedacceptednote
YYYY-MM-DD000-

Rules

  • A "memory win" means it cited a past judgement and saved a round of explanation, or avoided a repeated mistake. Name the entry id if possible.
  • A "disagreement" means it pushed back and you changed your mind. Record what changed.
  • If acceptance is zero for several days, stop and inspect the candidates instead of pushing through. Noise is a product bug.
  • Keep the store under 50 entries. If it grows faster, the proposal bar is too low.

Weekly check

niuse stats --days 7 --trend

Look for the direction, not the absolute number: acceptance should rise as the store matures, and the notes should become more specific.

Done

Ten rows, acceptance at or above 60%, at least three cited judgements, at least one recorded disagreement. Then M2-001 can move to review, and the next milestone is decided from the notes rather than from the backlog.

docs.title: Distribution notes
docs.summary: What installs today, why crates.io is blocked by path dependencies, and the decisions still open: dependency strategy, names, and license.
docs.body_html:
What works today

cargo install --git https://github.com/niuverse/niuse

This is also the path for people who only want the binary. It bypasses crates.io entirely.

Why crates.io is blocked

cargo package -p niuse fails:

error: all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging.
dependency `niucode-agent` does not specify a version

crates.io removes path specifications and expects the dependency to exist in the registry. Until that changes, only niuse-core is packageable on its own, and it is not useful without the CLI.

Options

OptionCostWhen
Publish the niucode-* crates first, then depend on versionsRelease coordination between the two repositoriesAfter niucode's embedding surface stabilizes
Switch to git dependencies with a pinned revisionEvery build fetches from GitHub; local co-development needs a patch overrideIf clean-checkout builds matter before publishing
Keep the CLI on cargo install --gitNo crates.io presence or docs.rs pageAcceptable while the tool is personal

The pinned-revision policy in compat is independent of this choice; it keeps the required CI reproducible either way.

Names

niuse, niuse-core, niuse-cli, and niucode were unclaimed on crates.io, npm, and PyPI when checked on 2026-10-21. Recheck immediately before publishing; registry names are first-come. The binary name is independent of the crate name, so a rename is recoverable.

License

Not chosen yet. crates.io requires a license or license-file, so publishing waits on that decision. The workspace repository field is set; the package warning now only complains about the missing license.

Checklist

  • Choose a license and add it to the workspace manifest.
  • Decide the niucode dependency strategy (publish first, git rev, or git-only install).
  • Recheck crate names and reserve them with a real release.
  • Add a release workflow that runs scripts/check.sh before publish.

docs.title: Dashboard guide
docs.summary: Sources, generation commands, the four views, and the ritual for adding modules, cards, and docs.
docs.body_html:
What this is

docs/index.html is the project's only architecture reading surface: Architecture, Work, Docs, and Decisions share one three-column shell. It is generated from repository sources, opens offline, and needs no server.

cargo xtask dashboard          # writes docs/index.html and docs/dashboard/model.json
cargo xtask dashboard --check  # CI: fails when generated output is stale or references break

Generation is deterministic: the same inputs produce the same HTML. receipt.json records the build time, git revision, and input list, but is not part of the staleness check.

Four views

  • Architecture (default): modules by layer, dependency arrows, contracts, and source. Selecting a module focuses its relations; status only shows implementation state, not progress.
  • Work: one file per card, a handoff surface filtered by milestone. No completion rates, WIP counts, or progress bars.
  • Docs: a Markdown index with a reading pane; supports deep links such as #/docs/adr-0001.
  • Decisions: ADR cards plus a kind = "decision" timeline. Completion logs do not belong here.

Sources

docs/
  index.html                # generated, committed, openable via file://
  dashboard/
    project.json            # project, milestones, layers, modules, relations, decisions
    template.html           # single-file shell
    style.css               # three-column layout and views
    app.js                  # framework-free rendering
    model.json              # generated
    receipt.json            # build receipt, gitignored
  board/
    M0-001-five-stores.md   # one card per file
  adr/
    0001-memory-layer.md
    0002-identity-layer.md
    0003-kernel-product-boundary.md
  architecture.md
  compat.md
  plan.md

Adding things

Add a module: add an entry to modules in project.json. Its layer must exist and paths must point at real files; any module not marked planned needs at least one existing path.

Add a work card: create a Markdown file under docs/board/. The TOML frontmatter must include id, title, status, milestone, size, and updated; done requires completed, and blocked requires blocked_reason.

Add a doc: any .md under docs/ with TOML frontmatter between +++ lines, including at least id, title, and kind. ADR status accepts only proposed, accepted, superseded, rejected, or draft.

Add a decision: write an ADR, or add a kind = "decision" event to project.json. When doing both, link them with refs.

Discipline

The board is read-only; the browser cannot write back. State changes go through the repository, so the board never becomes a second source of truth. Run --check before committing.
